cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema instance whose getSchemaNode() equals the supplied schemaNode and whose getCurrentUri() equals the supplied schemaUri
cases.description: Happy‑path test: a well‑formed JSON schema, a valid HTTP URI and a non‑null configuration should result in a successfully created JsonSchema object.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema instance; the internal ValidationContext should contain a default SchemaValidatorsConfig (i.e., config field is not null)
cases.description: When the config argument is null the method must still create a JsonSchema using the default configuration.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema instance whose current URI is null (or a fallback URI as defined by the implementation)
cases.description: The factory should accept a null base URI and still create a schema; this verifies that the method does not throw NPE when schemaUri is null.

cases.expected: throws NullPointerException
cases.description: createValidationContext is expected to require a non‑null JsonNode; passing null should result in an NPE.

group: Complex schema with nested subschemas – branch coverage in doCreate

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema where nested subschema objects are correctly created (e.g., schema.getSchemaNode().path("properties").path("address").has("properties"))
cases.description: A schema containing nested objects forces doCreate to traverse multiple branches (object, properties, subschema retrieval). This test ensures those internal branches are exercised.

cases.expected: returns a JsonSchema whose internal reference has been resolved via the URITranslator (i.e., the resulting schema is not a raw $ref node)
cases.description: When a schema contains a $ref, doCreate will invoke the URI translator and follow a different code path. This test validates that the translation occurs without throwing.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema whose getSchemaNode() is an empty ObjectNode and whose current URI equals the supplied schemaUri
cases.description: An empty JSON object is a valid (though trivial) schema. The factory should create a JsonSchema instance without throwing and preserve the supplied URI.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema whose getSchemaNode().isBoolean() is true and current URI equals the supplied file URI
cases.description: Draft‑07 allows a schema to be the literal boolean true. The method must accept such a node and produce a JsonSchema that reflects the boolean schema.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema; the underlying ValidationContext contains a config where isTypeLoose() == true
cases.description: Verifies that a non‑default configuration (typeLoose flag) is correctly stored in the ValidationContext and propagated to the created JsonSchema.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema; the schema’s current URI is null (or a fallback) and the internal ValidationContext uses a default SchemaValidatorsConfig
cases.description: Ensures the method gracefully handles both a null base URI and a null configuration, falling back to defaults without throwing.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema whose getCurrentUri().toString() contains the original fragment '#/definitions/foo'
cases.description: Checks that the factory does not strip the fragment part of the supplied URI; the fragment should be retained in the created schema’s current URI.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema whose getCurrentUri().getQuery() equals 'version=1'
cases.description: Ensures that URIs containing query strings are preserved unchanged in the created schema.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema; the schema node retains both $id and $schema fields and the factory normalizes the meta‑schema URI to the internal canonical form
cases.description: Verifies that when a schema declares its own $id and $schema (draft‑06), the factory records them correctly and applies any internal normalization logic.

group: Unsupported keyword – should still create schema

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema; validation of the schema itself is not performed here, so the unknown keyword does not cause an exception
cases.description: Ensures that the factory does not validate the content of the schema during creation; unknown keywords are tolerated at this stage.

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema where getSchemaNode().path("items").path("type").asText() equals 'string'
cases.description: Tests that an array schema with an embedded items subschema triggers the appropriate branch in doCreate and the items node is correctly attached.

group: Schema node missing explicit type – still creates

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema; the node is accepted even though the top‑level 'type' keyword is absent
cases.description: Ensures that the factory does not require a top‑level 'type' keyword; schemas that rely on implicit object type should still be instantiated.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: The factory expects the root schema node to be an object, array, or boolean. Supplying a numeric literal should cause an IllegalArgumentException during schema creation.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: A MissingNode represents the absence of a JSON value. Passing it as the schema root should trigger an IllegalArgumentException because the factory cannot build a JsonSchema from a non‑existent node.

group: Unsupported URI scheme – should raise exception

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException
cases.description: The factory’s internal URITranslator only supports http, https, file and classpath schemes. Supplying an unknown scheme should cause an IllegalArgumentException during URI translation.

group: Null configuration – internal NPE (if not tolerated)

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: If the implementation of ValidationContext.setConfig does not accept a null argument, passing null should result in a NullPointerException. This test captures that potential failure mode.
